Neither Conrad nor his father knew the rock's worth until three years later, when a jeweler realized it was gold. The discovery made North Carolina the country's leading gold producer for nearly 50 years, until the start of the California gold rush. Mining at Reed's mine began underground in 1831. Reed Gold Mine became a National Historic Landmark in 1895.

Article Title: A sealed early copy of Super Mario Bros. remained inside a Nintendo console bundle for decades; when discovered in 2026, it sold for $3 million
Article Text:
A representative image of old game consoles. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The cartridge belonged to an early production run

A representative image of old Mario game console. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The game remained inside its original Nintendo bundle

For nearly four decades, a copy of Super Mario Bros. was sealed inside an unopened Nintendo Entertainment System bundle. The copy was then discovered in 2026. The cartridge, preserved in its original packaging and accompanied by the Control Deck console with which it was originally bundled, eventually went to Heritage Auctions . It was sold for $3 million on 12 June 2026, setting a record for the highest price paid for a video game at a public auction.The cartridge received a PSA 9.6 A++ grade and was identified as a sealed example of Super Mario Bros.’ second production run. One of the things that made the find especially unusual was that it carried a short-lived gloss sticker seal associated with an early production variant. Meanwhile, the original console bundle itself had remained unopened. Contemporary reports suggest that only three sealed copies of this particular second-production variant were known, and the newly discovered one was considered the highest-graded of them.The NES and Super Mario Bros. dated to Nintendo’s early expansion of its home console business in the United States. It is, however, important to note that the console and cartridge should not be treated as though they came from the exact same production moment. Heritage Auctions’ description identifies the bundle as a 1985-styled USA Nintendo NES Control Deck release distributed in 1986.Meanwhile, the Super Mario Bros. cartridge itself is described as a second-production gloss-sticker example. Nintendo reportedly adopted the gloss sticker in early 1986, after the short-lived matte sticker used on launch copies from its October 1985 test market.The game itself is not a first-production copy. Instead, it is a second-production example which has been described as the earliest confirmed sealed copy because no sealed first-production example is currently known. Aside from the newly discovered one, the other two have received VGA 80 and Wata 9.4 A++ grades. The production history, therefore, provides an explanation for why a very common game could turn into an exceptionally rare collectable in one particular form.The preservation of the cartridge was equally unconventional, as the original inner packaging remained intact. The console and its components had never even been removed from their plastic. The auction lot contained the Control Deck with which the Super Mario Bros. cartridge had originally been packaged. This indicates that the game had not been passed down between collectors; instead, it remained inside the original packaging, secured.Following its discovery two months prior to the sale, Heritage placed the cartridge and Control Deck together in its 12-13 June 2026 Video Games Signature Auction as Lot 28025. The auction house promoted the game as the earliest confirmed sealed edition of Super Mario Bros. and highlighted its condition alongside the circumstances of its discovery. The auction resulted in a $3 million sale. This had surpassed the previous $2 million record established by a private sale in 2021.The price of the copy is, therefore, tied to several aspects rather than just the age of the cartridge. Likely millions of people played the game, but this example belonged to a narrowly defined production variant, offering unparalleled historical provenance due to the un-boxing sequence. Additionally, its PSA 9.6 A++ grade further distinguished it from other surviving sealed copies of the same variant.
Article Summary: Super Mario Bros. was discovered inside an unopened Nintendo Entertainment System bundle. The cartridge belonged to an early production run of the game. It was sold for $3 million on 12 June 2026, setting a record for the highest price paid for a video game at a public auction.

Article Title: In 2014, a sheriff’s sale turned up an Apple-1 whose owner had fled the country; the buyer paid without realising exactly what it was, and Christie's sold it for $365,000
Article Text:
A running Apple I, with a keyboard and monitor connected. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The Apple-1 began when Apple was still a small operation

This machine’s journey from Ricketts to a Virginia sheriff

Original 1976 Apple 1 Computer in a briefcase. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The First Apple

Christie’s tested the computer before putting it up for sale

In December 2014, a significant Apple-1 computer was sold by Christie’s in New York for $365,000. The auction took place 10 years after Bob Luther attended a sheriff’s sale in Virginia in 2004 and bought an old computer for $7,600. While he was aware that he was acquiring something that was connected to early computers, he had initially not understood the significance of the machine. Christie’s records identify the machine as the “Ricketts Apple-1,” after its original owner, Charles Ricketts. The computer’s history was traced back to its purchase from Jobs in 1976 through later owners and finally to Luther.Ricketts had retained documents connecting the machine to Apple’s earliest days. Among them was a primarily cancelled $600 check dated 27 July 1976, made payable to Apple Computer. Later on, Ricketts annotated the check to record that he had bought the computer from Steve Jobs at his parents’ garage in Los Altos. Eventually, this document helped turn an old circuit board into a valuable artefact.In 1976, Steve Wozniak designed the Apple-1 and Steve Jobs marketed it. The Computer History Museum records that Wozniak finished the Apple-1 that year and that, alongside Jobs, they secured an order for 50 assembled systems from the Byte Shop in Mountain View, California. Around 200 Apple-1 boards were ultimately sold before the company moved on to the Apple II.The initial machine was very different from the Macintosh and later Apple computers.The Apple-1 was a single-board computer for hobbyists instead of being a complete consumer desktop system; buyers needed additional equipment, including a keyboard and display, to use it as a functioning computer. Though most of these machines were sold via the Byte Shop, Ricketts’ machine had a different story. The auction house described it as the only known surviving Apple-1 with documentation indicating that it was sold directly by Steve Jobs to an individual from his family’s garage.In 1976, Ricketts reportedly acquired the computer for $600. The surviving cancelled check was made payable to Apple Computer instead of Jobs personally. But Ricketts subsequently wrote on it that the machine was purchased from Jobs himself at the family garage. These documents became crucial because Apple-1’s history is usually difficult to construct for many individual machines. In this case, the computer was accompanied by contemporary paperwork that connected it to a named buyer, a specific date and an early Apple location, including a second cancelled check for $193 dated 5 August 1976, which Ricketts annotated as relating to software programmed by Steve Jobs.The auction house’s provenance records that the Apple-1 eventually passed from Ricketts to his son, and then lists Neil Brian Goldberg of Computer Jones and Bruce Waldack, founder of DigitalNation, as owners in 1999. Waldack later experienced financial problems. Reports suggest that he lost his fortune, defaulted on payments for his Learjet and fled to Argentina. Subsequently, his property in Virginia was subjected to a sheriff’s sale, with the Apple-1 being one of the properties that was offered at a self-storage facility in 2004.Through an advertisement, Luther encountered the sale and ultimately purchased the Apple-1 for $7,600 on 14 December 2004. Luther’s purchase did not instantly turn the computer into a valuable collectable. What made things more interesting was the history he subsequently investigated. He spent years tracing the machine’s provenance and interviewing people connected to Apple’s early years. Luther’s research eventually became the basis for his 2013 book,. The two cancelled checks, alongside Luther’s book that documented his efforts to investigate the machine and the people connected with its past, helped establish Apple-1’s provenance.The Apple-1 was not merely an inert historical object. In October 2014, Apple-1 specialist Corey Cohen serviced and successfully started the machine, with reports claiming that Cohen ran the original Apple BASIC program and an original Apple-1 Star Trek game to test it. An original Apple-1 operating manual, a keyboard housed in a wooden case, power equipment and the two 1976 checks were found in the lot.On 3 November 2014, Christie’s announced the auction , describing the machine as the only known surviving Apple-1 documented as having been sold directly by Jobs to an individual. The auction house estimated that it could sell for $400,000 to $600,000. On 11 December 2014, the auction took place in New York, and it was sold for $365,000, below what was originally estimated.
Article Summary: In December 2014, a significant Apple-1 computer was sold by Christie's in New York for $365,000. The auction took place 10 years after Bob Luther attended a sheriff’s sale in Virginia in 2004 and bought an old computer for $7,600. While he was aware that he was acquiring something that was connected to early computers, he had initially not understood the significance of the machine. He spent years tracing the machine's provenance and interviewing people connected to Apple's early years. The computer's history was traced back to its purchase from Steve Jobs in 1976 through later owners.

Article Title: Las Vegas company surprises nearly 10,000 workers with more than $70 million in stock; each gets $1,000 for every year they have worked there
Article Text:
Las Vegas company surprises nearly 10,000 workers with more than $70 million in stock (Image Credit: Red Rock Resorts)

Nearly 10,000 employees receive stock

Long-serving employees receive tens of thousands of dollars

The stock award covered nearly 10,000 Station Casinos team members, most of whom are based in Southern Nevada (Image Credit: Red Rock Resorts)

Surprise announcement marks 50 years in Las Vegas

Company says award reflects employee contribution

From local casino to five decades of operations

Nearly 10,000 employees of Las Vegas-based Station Casinos received an unexpected financial reward as the company marked its 50th anniversary. According to a September 9 announcement from Red Rock Resorts, the parent company of Station Casinos, eligible full and part-time employees received more than $70 million worth of Red Rock Resorts Class A stock, calculated at $1,000 for every year of service. The announcement was made during a surprise celebration at Red Rock Casino Resort & Spa, where company executives revealed the award to employees. The stock grants recognise workers across the company, with some long-serving employees receiving tens of thousands of dollars in shares.The stock award covered nearly 10,000 Station Casinos team members, most of whom are based in Southern Nevada. Employees who were working for the company as of September 9, 2026, were eligible for the award. Rather than providing the same amount to every employee, Station Casinos based the value of each grant on the individual's length of service. Under the programme, workers received $1,000 in Red Rock Resorts Class A stock for every year they had worked for the company. Altogether, the grants were valued at more than $70 million.The announcement came during an event at Red Rock Casino Resort & Spa, where Red Rock Resorts Chairman and CEO Frank Fertitta III and Vice Chairman Lorenzo Fertitta revealed the surprise to employees gathered for the company's anniversary celebration.Because the award was tied directly to years of service, some of Station Casinos' longest-serving employees received particularly large stock grants. One of them is Ida Johnson, who began working for the company in 1977. Based on the $1,000-per-year formula, Johnson received $49,000 worth of Red Rock Resorts stock.The company said seven team members who started working in the 1970s at what was then Bingo Palace and remain with the company today each received more than $45,000 in equity. The awards therefore vary considerably depending on an employee's tenure. A worker with 10 years of service, for example, would receive $10,000 worth of stock under the announced formula, while someone with several decades at the company could receive many times that amount.The stock distribution formed the centrepiece of Station Casinos' 50th anniversary celebrations. The company's anniversary programme began on July 1 at Palace Station, the property where its story began. The opening celebration included a fireworks and drone show, along with the launch of a new brand identity and the campaign "From Vegas, For Vegas, Always Vegas."Events continued throughout the summer across the Las Vegas Valley. According to Red Rock Resorts, the anniversary programme included live entertainment, commemorative gaming and food-and-beverage offerings, vintage photo booths, employee appreciation events and community volunteer initiatives. The September 9 gathering brought the anniversary programme to a close, while also paying tribute to company founder Frank Fertitta Jr. , Station Casinos' history in Las Vegas and employees who have worked for the company over the past five decades.Speaking at the surprise anniversary ceremony at Red Rock Casino Resort & Spa, Frank Fertitta III, Chairman and CEO of Red Rock Resorts, said the company's founding principles included serving the local community, providing value and taking care of its employees. He described the stock award as a recognition of the people who had helped build Station Casinos over its first 50 years. Lorenzo Fertitta similarly described the award as an investment in the company's nearly 10,000 team members and highlighted their role in building relationships with guests and the Las Vegas community.The surprise element added another dimension to the celebration. Employees arrived at the September 9 event without knowing that the company was preparing to distribute such a large stock award. The announcement meant that the anniversary celebration was not only about marking Station Casinos' history but also about providing employees with Red Rock Resorts stock tied to their years of service.Station Casinos has grown into a major gaming and entertainment operator serving the Las Vegas Valley. Its properties include Red Rock Casino Resort & Spa, Green Valley Ranch Resort Spa Casino, Durango Casino & Resort, Palace Station, Boulder Station, Sunset Station and several Wildfire properties. The company said the 50th anniversary celebration was intended to recognise both its development in Las Vegas and the employees who contributed to that history.With more than $70 million in Red Rock Resorts Class A stock distributed, the anniversary has also become a milestone for thousands of current employees. For workers who have spent decades with Station Casinos, the value of the award is directly tied to the length of time they have remained with the company, making the 50th anniversary celebration a recognition of their years of service as well as the company's history.
Article Summary: Las Vegas company surprises nearly 10,000 workers with more than $70 million in stock. Stock grants recognise workers across the company, with some long-serving employees receiving tens of thousands of dollars in shares. The stock distribution formed the centrepiece of Station Casinos' 50th anniversary celebrations.

Article Title: In 1945, Oklahoma opened a nearly 4,900-foot bridge across Lake Texoma; 81 years later a record $408 million project has begun to build its replacement while the old bridge stays open
Article Text: More than eight decades after the Roosevelt Bridge first carried traffic across Lake Texoma, Oklahoma has begun work on a massive replacement project that will reshape one of the region’s most important transportation links. The Oklahoma Department of Transportation (ODOT) says the more than $408 million project will replace the aging US-70 bridge while keeping the existing structure open throughout construction. Details from ODOT, Equipment World and local broadcaster KXII confirm the project’s record scale, historic origins and planned 2029 completion.The US-70 Roosevelt Bridge opened in 1945, connecting Bryan and Marshall counties across Lake Texoma in southeastern Oklahoma. The original structure stretches roughly 4,900 feet and consists of 87 spans, including a distinctive Warren through-truss central span. ODOT records describe that central span as the only surviving example of its type on Oklahoma’s highway system with a polygonal top chord.Now, 81 years after its opening, the bridge is approaching the end of its useful life. An analysis found the structure at risk of becoming structurally deficient and classified it as functionally obsolete, prompting years of planning for a modern replacement.The new project represents one of Oklahoma’s largest bridge investments. The contract, valued at $408 million, was awarded to a joint venture between Zachry Construction and Traylor Bros. The project is supported by state funding and a $124 million federal Bridge Investment Program grant, which ODOT has described as the largest federal transportation grant awarded in Oklahoma for the project.The replacement will feature a new four-lane bridge across Lake Texoma, along with improvements to the US-70 approaches. The design also calls for full shoulders, improved lighting and a pedestrian path, addressing safety and capacity concerns on the existing crossing.The bridge is particularly important because US-70 serves as a regional connection between southern Oklahoma and northern Texas, supporting daily commuting, freight movement, tourism and other economic activity. Latest figures show more than 11,000 vehicles use the corridor each day.Construction is being delivered through a modified progressive design-build approach, a method being used for the first time. The process allows the transportation department and its design-build team to work together during design and construction planning, with the aim of improving the project’s schedule, design and cost efficiency.Work is already underway around the site. Crews have been clearing trees and preparing the construction area, while barges have begun drilling into the lakebed to investigate the ground conditions where the new bridge’s piers will be anchored. Lake Texoma reaches depths of about 65 feet near the existing bridge, adding another layer of engineering complexity to the project.The new bridge will be built while traffic continues to use the old one. That means drivers will not immediately lose the existing US-70 crossing as construction progresses. Once the replacement is finished, the new structure is expected to provide four lanes of modern roadway, improving reliability and safety for motorists travelling between Oklahoma and Texas.Construction is expected to continue for roughly three years, with the new bridge scheduled for completion in fall 2029. The project therefore marks more than the replacement of an aging piece of infrastructure: it represents the transition from a bridge that has served the region since the postwar era to a new crossing designed to carry traffic for decades to come.
Article Summary: The US-70 Roosevelt Bridge opened in 1945, connecting Bryan and Marshall counties across Lake Texoma in southeastern Oklahoma. The original structure stretches roughly 4,900 feet and consists of 87 spans, including a distinctive Warren through-truss central span. An analysis found the structure at risk of becoming structurally deficient and classified it as functionally obsolete, prompting years of planning for a modern replacement.

Article Title: In July, Montana protected 34,610 acres in the Cabinet Mountains; a proposed second phase would add 13,297 acres, creating a 47,907-acre conservation corridor with permanent public access
Article Text:
Development rights would be permanently restricted

A multimillion-dollar second phase

Why the landscape matters

For generations, the forests of northwest Montana have been more than timberland. They have provided habitat for wildlife, working forests for local communities and places where people hunt, hike and explore. Now, state officials are working to give a large stretch of that landscape permanent protection. According to Western News and Daily Inter Lake, Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks has begun the second and final phase of the Upper Thompson Conservation Easement, a project that could ultimately place development restrictions on 47,907 acres of private timberland in the Cabinet Mountains. The first 34,610 acres were secured in July, while another 13,297 acres are now under consideration. The proposed second phase covers timberland in the Little Thompson River, Smiley Creek and Buffalo Bill Creek drainages. Under the agreement, FWP would acquire the development rights from Green Diamond Montana Timberlands, while the company would continue to own and manage the property.That distinction is important. The land would not become a state-owned preserve, and timber operations would not end. Green Diamond would be able to continue harvesting timber under the terms of the easement, with the area currently producing about 1.6 million board feet of timber each year, according to the state’s environmental assessment.What would change is what could happen to the land in the future.The proposed easement would prevent Green Diamond and future owners from extensively developing or subdividing the property. At the same time, it would establish permanent public access for activities including hunting, trapping, hiking and other outdoor recreation.That builds on the first phase of the project. Montana’s Fish and Wildlife Commission approved the purchase of the initial 34,610-acre Upper Thompson Conservation Easement in June, and the deal closed in July. The first phase protects wildlife habitat and landscape connectivity while allowing continued sustainable timber management. Together, the two phases would create a single 47,907-acre conservation easement across the Upper Thompson River landscape.The second phase has been appraised at approximately $17.1 million. Green Diamond has committed nearly $5.75 million in in-kind value, reducing the amount the state and its partners would need to raise to about $11.35 million.Funding is expected to come from a combination of sources, including the U.S. Forest Service’s Forest Legacy Program, the Trust for Public Land, Avista, NorthWestern Energy and the Montana Fish and Wildlife Conservation Trust. FWP is expected to contribute about $150,000 from the state conservation trust, according to the latest proposal.The broader project has taken years to assemble. The first phase alone was supported by $13 million from the Forest Legacy Program, along with contributions from the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation, Montana Fish and Wildlife Conservation Trust, the Trust for Public Land and Green Diamond.The Upper Thompson area forms part of a much larger network of forests and protected lands in northwest Montana. The conservation easement is designed to maintain connections between wildlife habitats while keeping the land available as a working forest.The first phase also secured recreational access that had previously depended on voluntary arrangements. With the easement in place, public access becomes a permanent condition of the protected property rather than something that could potentially change with a future owner. The second phase is not final yet.FWP initiated the process on August 28 and is currently seeking public input. A public hearing is scheduled for 6 p.m. on September 23 at Plains High School, while written comments on the proposed acquisition are being accepted until 5 p.m. on September 26.If approved and fully funded, the additional 13,297 acres would complete a conservation effort covering nearly 48,000 acres of Montana timberland, protecting its development rights while allowing the forests to remain working landscapes and keeping them open to the public.
Article Summary: Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks has begun the second and final phase of the Upper Thompson Conservation Easement. The project could ultimately place development restrictions on 47,907 acres of private timberland in the Cabinet Mountains. The first 34,610 acres were secured in July, while another 13,297 acres are now under consideration.

Article Title: Wisconsin farmer Brit Thompson turns a vintage Airstream trailer into an Airbnb, now the rental income outpaces beef and lamb sales: ‘I can make $100 an hour cleaning’
Article Text:
Representative image

The rise of agritourism

Growing trend

A vintage Airstream trailer parked on a Wisconsin pasture may not sound like a financial lifeline, at least not six years ago. But it is now for Brit Thompson, 33, who runs Pink River Ranch in Wisconsin. She converted her vintage Airstream trailer into an Airbnb , and most of her guests are Chicago-area professionals looking for countryside experiences.Thompson is a farmer, but the unstable economy pushed her to think beyond the box. "I don't want to be out there working my b**t off for $5 an hour when I can make $100 cleaning the Airstream for an hour,” she told MarketScreener. For farmers like Thompson, that difference matters. It can take far longer to earn the same amount by selling beef and lamb through restaurants or farmers' markets.Brit Thompson, who also raises animals for meat on her farm, is one of many farmers turning to agricultural tourism, a $4.5 billion industry, according to data from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA). Her trailer now doubles as an Airbnb, offering overnight stays. The decline in income from farming and the rising demand for rural experiences have motivated many farmers in the US to step into tourism.Thompson's ranch sits down the road in Blanchardville, surrounded by Highland cattle, Icelandic sheep, and the kind of landscape that urbanites yearn for. Most of her bookings come from urban areas, including Chicago. Professionals seeking weekend escapes book the stay. Guests visit almost every week during the peak season, drawn by spring-fed trout streams, forested hiking trails, and unpolluted night skies. Needless to say, the income surpasses what her livestock operation generates. This also opens new opportunities for Thompson: she teaches her guests about sustainable grazing, as well as fishing from her riverbank with her five-year-old daughter, who reels in fat catfish with a miniature hot-pink fishing rod.Thompson is far from alone in recognising the potential of agritourism. Farmers across the US are making the same calculation. They are turning corn mazes, pumpkin patches, farmstays, and cabin rentals into essential revenue streams as traditional agriculture withers. This revenue is nowhere comparable to what most of them make from farming alone. For families trying to hold on to their land, these enterprises mean a lot. They no longer have to sell their land.Farm income has dropped 23% from 2022, according to data from the USDA. This is one of the steepest declines in history, and the American Farm Bureau confirms that the agricultural economy is in recession.Commodity prices for corn and soy hit four-year lows last year. But input costs for seeds, fertiliser, and labour remain punishingly high. Interest rates have climbed. Potential tariffs loom. The maths for row-crop farmers has never been worse."You cannot survive as a family farm only farming," Catherine Topel, 56, a North Carolina hog producer who hosts an Airbnb cabin and campsites through HipCamp, told Reuters."The cabins, the camping – it makes you sustainable and resilient in hard times, and it gives you flexibility to enter into other enterprises instead of toeing the line of what your dad did and what your dad's dad did."Kaylee Heap, 35, co-manager of Heap's Giant Pumpkin Farm in Illinois, where guests pick sunflowers and pumpkins in autumn, ride hayrides, and navigate corn mazes, agrees. "We're able to weather some of these tighter or negative margin years because we've diversified the way we earn money," Kaylee Heap told the news agency. "It's the reason we diversified. If we just focused on row crops, we’d be having a different conversation. "Agritourism flourished during the pandemic. People living in cities were in search of socially distanced holiday options, and rural properties offered exactly that. But this wasn't a temporary trend. The number of farmstays listed on short-term rental platforms jumped 77% over five years, roughly double the growth rate of overall listings. Airbnb, HipCamp, Harvest Hosts, and The Dyrt all report substantial increases in farmstay inventory. Not every property is suited for this type of tourism. Countryside properties are at the top of the list, as are secluded locations surrounded by nature.The trend is here to stay, according to Ryan Pesch, an extension educator at the University of Minnesota. “The younger generation finds the farm doesn't have to be this long litany of depression and bad prices. They say: 'Why don't we do this other thing?’ They see opportunities and entrepreneurship," he told Reuters.
Article Summary: Farm income has dropped 23% from 2022, according to data from the USDA. American Farm Bureau confirms that the agricultural economy is in recession. Number of farmstays listed on short-term rental platforms jumped 77% over five years, roughly double rate of overall listings.

Article Title: BLA claims killing 43 Pakistan military personnel past week
Article Text:
BLA said it imposed multi-hour blockades on Besima-Kapuk and Quetta-Taftan trade routes

Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has claimed responsibility for 13 coordinated attacks across Balochistan over the past week, saying its fighters killed 43 Pakistani military and state-affiliated "Death Squad" personnel. The rebel group acknowledged losing 10 fighters.BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the operations, involving road blockades, targeted strikes, took place in Besima, Kharan, Panjgur, Chagai, Surab, Qila Abdullah and Awaran, where it claimed two Pakistani army soldiers were killed.According to the statement, BLA said it imposed multi-hour blockades on Besima-Kapuk and Quetta-Taftan trade routes to conduct snap checks and restrict troop movements. It claimed 25 personnel were killed on Sept 13 in an ambush on state-aligned local militias in Sultan Charak, Qila Abdullah, followed by a four-hour clash with army reinforcements.The group also claimed its "Fateh Squad" killed nine soldiers in Lasbela, while another operation targeted four military intelligence operatives in Jiwani. It said fighters destroyed surveillance equipment in Panjgur and burnt machinery at a lithium extraction site in Machil under its "economic blockade". BLA said it would continue armed resistance until Pakistani security forces withdrew from the region entirely. On Monday, it released a video purportedly showing fighters seizing 14 posts on Quetta-Taftan Highway.
Article Summary: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claims responsibility for 13 coordinated attacks across Balochistan over the past week. It says its fighters killed 43 Pakistani military and state-affiliated "Death Squad" personnel. BLA said it would continue armed resistance until Pakistani security forces withdrew from the region entirely.

Article Title: 'It is defensive, nothing aggressive': Pak scrambles to define Mecca pact after Houthi attack
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan's military spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry

What happens if Saudi Arabia is attacked?

Not a Muslim military bloc

Pakistan says pact does not compete with China ties

Why Pakistan is walking a diplomatic tightrope

Pakistan’s military has rushed to give a definition to the newly formed Mecca Defence Alliance, saying the pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey is meant for collective deterrence and has “no regional aspirations”, even as questions grow over how the agreement would work if one of its members comes under attack.Pakistan’s inter-services public relations (ISPR) director general Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, speaking to Al Arabiya, said the agreement was “defensive” and “complementary” to the three countries’ existing alliances and relationships.“It is defensive. There’s nothing aggressive. There are no regional aspirations. It is collective deterrence,” Chaudhry said.The comments come as the pact faces questions over its first potential test. The alliance has been put under scrutiny amid the conflict involving Saudi Arabia and Houthi forces, with uncertainty over whether Riyadh has sought military assistance from Islamabad and how Pakistan would respond if it did.The pact was signed on August 7 and says an attack on one member would be treated as an attack on all. Pakistan is to initially head its secretariat for three years.Also read: Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pakistan expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on kingdom Chaudhry was pressed on precisely that question during the Al Arabiya interview: whether Pakistan had a mutual defence obligation under the agreement and what it would actually do if one of the members came under attack.He said the publicly released text made the mutual defence commitment clear, but stressed that the operational details of how such a commitment would be implemented were classified.“What you’re asking is the how part — how we are going to defend Pakistan against any aggression,” he said, adding that such decisions would be for the three countries to make.The distinction is significant because the pact has not yet been tested in an actual conflict. The first major test could become the escalating Houthi-Saudi confrontation, with questions remaining over when an attack would trigger the alliance and what form military assistance would take.The uncertainty is also not entirely new. Pakistan’s parliament had unanimously rejected a request in 2015 to send troops to join the Saudi-led coalition against the Houthis. Pakistan also shares a long border with Iran, giving Islamabad an additional security consideration as it navigates its relationship with Riyadh and Tehran.Chaudhry also rejected the idea that the Mecca Defence Alliance was being designed as a broader Muslim military bloc.“There is nothing in the pact that says that it is a Muslim alliance,” he said, describing it instead as an arrangement aimed at regional stability.He said other countries could potentially join if they shared the principles of non-aggression, non-interference and collective deterrence, but stressed that any expansion would be a decision for the leaders of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey.The comments come amid speculation about possible expansion of the grouping. Turkey had previously suggested Egypt could join, although Cairo has not confirmed any such move. Pakistan’s foreign office has meanwhile said the immediate priority was to consolidate the new organisation before considering expansion.Chaudhry also sought to reassure Beijing that the new arrangement was not aimed at competing with Pakistan’s relationship with China.Asked whether the alliance complemented or competed with Islamabad’s ties with Beijing, he said it was complementary.He argued that Pakistan’s relationships with Saudi Arabia and Turkey were longstanding and that the three countries also maintained good relations with China.“Everyone understands that this is defensive,” Chaudhry said, adding that the pact was intended to maintain “stability and peace in the region”.The military spokesperson was also asked whether the defence pact complicated Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between the US and Iran amid the ongoing Middle East conflict.Chaudhry rejected that suggestion, saying the pact formalised longstanding relationships rather than creating a new strategic alignment against another country.He described Pakistan as being in a “unique position” because of its engagement with different countries and said Islamabad could therefore act as an “objective arbiter of peace” and an “honest broker”.Pakistan, he said, wanted a negotiated and peaceful resolution rather than a military solution.That position is particularly relevant as Islamabad balances its strategic relationship with Saudi Arabia with its geographic proximity to Iran.Chaudhry said Pakistan's decision to mediate was driven by a desire for regional peace and that the country would continue engaging the parties involved.
Article Summary: Pakistan's military has given a definition to the newly formed Mecca Defence Alliance. The pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey is meant for collective deterrence. Pakistan’s inter-services public relations director general Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said the agreement was “defensive” and “complementary” to the three countries’ existing alliances.

Article Title: Pakistan ministers warn of energy crisis; Shehbaz government struggles as fuel prices break records
Article Text:
Shehbaz ministers warn of energy crisis as Pakistan fuel prices surge

Fuel shock puts Shehbaz government under pressure

Pakistan is facing a widening energy crunch as disruptions around key Gulf shipping routes push up global oil prices, fuel costs surge and the government weighs measures to curb petroleum consumption.Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s government is facing pressure on multiple fronts, with ministers warning about the impact of disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab El-Mandeb while trying to shield consumers from soaring fuel prices.Petrol prices were raised by PKR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel by PKR 6.41 per litre on Tuesday night, taking petrol to PKR 384.34 per litre and HSD to PKR 415.83 per litre.The sharp increases have raised concerns about how long Pakistan can absorb the impact of the global oil shock, with climate change minister Musadik Malik saying the government was trying to absorb part of the increase through its fuel relief scheme.Under the scheme, motorcyclists would receive subsidised petrol for up to five litres a week, while car owners would get relief on up to 10 litres every 10 days. Malik said the assistance would not fully offset the increase in fuel prices but represented the maximum burden the economy could currently absorb.Energy minister Awais Leghari also sounded the alarm over the supply situation, saying Pakistan had managed to keep its power plants running despite disruptions by maximising the use of domestic energy resources.In August, 72% of Pakistan’s electricity generation came from domestic sources, including hydropower, local coal, nuclear power, local gas, wind and solar, while 28% came from imported coal and RLNG.Leghari said disruptions to RLNG supplies had pushed spot cargo prices to $23.25 per MMBtu. Increased use of domestic gas for power generation helped Pakistan avoid buying more expensive RLNG, he said.Without the additional domestic gas, Pakistan could have faced another hour of load shedding, while greater reliance on furnace oil or imported RLNG could have increased consumer tariffs by around PKR 10.6 billion, according to the minister.As the energy crisis deepens, the government is considering ways to reduce petroleum consumption, including the possibility of a “smart lockdown”.Such measures were used during the peak of the US-Iran war, including a four-day working week and early closure of markets. Information minister Atta Tarar had also indicated that austerity measures could be brought back if the regional situation worsened.However, Malik rejected reports that a smart lockdown was currently being discussed, saying no such discussions had taken place.The government is simultaneously expanding its fuel relief programme. A National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy, chaired by deputy prime minister Ishaq Dar, has directed that payments to fuel stations be processed within 24 hours. The scheme, initially piloted in Islamabad, is being rolled out across Pakistan.The fuel shock is also creating political pressure. Jamaat-i-Islami has threatened nationwide demonstrations next week if fuel prices are not reduced.Pakistan has also switched to a daily petroleum pricing mechanism, introduced in July to replace the previous weekly system, as global oil prices became increasingly volatile amid geopolitical tensions.The crisis sharpens as Saudi Arabia has shut its East-West oil pipeline after it came under aerial attack, adding to concerns over global supplies.
Article Summary: Petrol prices were raised by PKR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel by 6.41. The sharp increases have raised concerns about how long Pakistan can absorb the impact of the global oil shock. The government is considering ways to reduce petroleum consumption, including the possibility of a ‘smart lockdown’

Article Title: 'Our father being slowly killed': Imran Khan's sons accuse Pakistan's Asim Munir of vendetta
Article Text:
Imran Khan's sons: Sulaiman Khan (left) and Kasim Khan (Photo: The Times)

The sons of jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan have accused army chief Asim Munir of pursuing a "personal vendetta" against their father, alleging that his prison conditions amount to mental and physical torture.Speaking to The Guardian, Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, said they were “deeply” concerned about the health of their 73-year-old father, who has been held at Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023.Khan is serving a 14-year sentence in a corruption case. His sons said they had not been allowed to speak to him for more than six months and had also been prevented from travelling from the UK to Pakistan to seek his release.The allegations come ahead of a Supreme Court ruling on Wednesday in a case alleging that the Pakistan government has failed to comply with a court order allowing Khan private hospital treatment for an eye condition and permitting family visits and communication.Sulaiman alleged that his father had been denied human contact, new books, access to family and an independent doctor. He also said Khan’s eye condition had been neglected for months, potentially resulting in severe loss of sight in one eye."It’s very clear this is being driven by personal grudge," Sulaiman told The Guardian, alleging that Khan was being treated harshly on Munir’s orders.Khan had reportedly demoted Munir during his tenure as prime minister, and tensions between the two were widely known. Munir became army chief in 2022, while Khan’s political conflict with the military establishment intensified.Kasim alleged that the family believed their father was being “slowly killed” in prison and said they feared restrictions on him could become harsher when international pressure eased.The allegations follow a recent dispute over Khan’s medical treatment. Last month, the Supreme Court ruled that he should be taken to a private hospital for treatment of a blood clot in a retinal vein. His family said the condition had severely affected the sight in his right eye.Khan was instead briefly taken to a government hospital, where he received injections before being declared fit to return to prison, according to The Guardian.The Pakistan government has rejected the allegations, calling them “fake propaganda”. It said Khan was being kept in adequate conditions and had access to home-cooked food, nuts, bottled water, exercise equipment, family visits and regular medical examinations.“The government of Pakistan categorically rejects allegations that the convicted prisoner is being subjected to punitive solitary confinement, cruelty or deprivation,” it said.The United Nations has previously said Khan’s prolonged detention violates international law, while the UN special rapporteur on torture has said his solitary confinement and detention conditions could amount to psychological torture.
Article Summary: Imran Khan is serving a 14-year sentence in a corruption case. His sons have accused army chief Asim Munir of pursuing a "personal vendetta" They say they have not been allowed to speak to him for more than six months. The Pakistan government has rejected the allegations.

Article Title: Pakistan military jets strike Kalat in fresh Balochistan attacks: Report
Article Text:
Balochistan: Pakistani aircraft reportedly conduct airstrikes in Kalat

Drone, helicopter attacks also reported

Pakistani military aircraft reportedly carried out airstrikes at two locations in Kalat on Monday, a day after a drone allegedly targeted a vehicle in Manguchar, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP).A jet aircraft reportedly conducted an airstrike in the Chappar area of Kalat, where a powerful blast was heard. There was no immediate information about casualties or the extent of damage.Another explosion was reported near Took and Dasht-e-Goran. The exact location of the blast could not immediately be confirmed, though jet aircraft were reportedly seen flying over the area around the time of the explosion, news agency ANI cited.On Sunday, a drone reportedly targeted a vehicle in Manguchar. Gunship helicopters also allegedly shelled Rudeenjo and nearby areas for several hours on Sunday, while quadcopter attacks were reported from parts of the district.Communication disruptions and movement restrictions in the affected areas have made it difficult to independently verify the reports or obtain comprehensive details about casualties and damage, TBP said.The reported attacks come amid a series of military operations and aerial strikes across Balochistan in recent weeks, with several incidents triggering allegations of civilian casualties.
Article Summary: Pakistani military aircraft reportedly carried out airstrikes at two locations in Kalat on Monday. On Sunday, a drone allegedly targeted a vehicle in Manguchar. Gunship helicopters also allegedly shelled Rudeenjo and nearby areas for several hours on Sunday.

Article Title: Pak ups reward for Masood Azhar by PKR 20L ahead of FATF meet
Article Text: Taking its duplicity on combating terror to farcical levels, Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has declared a reward of PKR 70 lakh on UN-designated terrorist Maulana Masood Azhar while calling him a "fugitive". The move comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) meeting next month.Pakistan had initially included Azhar in its 'red book' in 2021, setting a bounty of PKR 50 lakh. With apprehensions of being placed back on the FATF's 'grey list', Pakistan has now raised the reward by an additional PKR 20 lakh after five years.The move comes despite Islamabad's long-standing falsehood that Azhar escaped to Afghanistan and was no longer in the country. Even after key family members overseeing Jaish-e-Mohammed operations were eliminated in Operation Sindoor, Pakistan has remained unwilling to acknowledge his presence on its territory or extradite him to India. The assessment of Indian agencies is that he is based in the Sindh province but is often moved to different locations by the ISI to escape an assassination bid.Azhar, who is believed to have escaped the attack on the JeM's headquarters in Markaz Subhanallah, Bahawalpur, is wanted in India in connection with several attacks, including the 2019 Pulwama bombing in which 40 CRPF personnel were killed.Azhar's profile in the 'red book', which lists Pakistan's most-wanted fugitives and terrorists, doesn't mention any details including national ID card or passport number, place of birth, sect or any identification mark."The federal govt of Pakistan is offering a reward of Rs 70,00,000 for information directly leading to apprehension or conviction of Masood Azhar, the son of Khuda Baksh," it says.As it did in 2021, Pakistan has also maintained that the 26/11 Mumbai attack planners were not on its soil, as per the book. It has retained the profiles of 17 terrorists involved in the planning and financing of the Mumbai attacks, continued from 2021, but the photographs and details of two of the terrorists - Abdul Rehman and Muhammad Khan - have been removed this time. Khan had provided the boat used in the attack.The 'red book' in Pakistan is an official document published by law enforcement agencies to 'list and track' the country's most-wanted fugitives and high-profile terrorists.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has declared a reward of PKR 70 lakh on UN-designated terrorist Maulana Masood Azhar. The move comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) meeting next month. Azhar is wanted in India in connection with several attacks, including the 2019 Pulwama bombing.

Article Title: Pakistan weighs austerity measures as US-Iran war drives up fuel prices
Article Text: Pakistan may bring back austerity measures to reduce fuel consumption as renewed fighting in West Asia drives up global oil prices, as news agency PTI cited Pak information minister Ataullah Tarar Monday.Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to examine which of the measures introduced earlier this year can be brought back, Tarar said at a press briefing attended by information technology minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja and petroleum minister Ali Pervaiz Malik."Austerity measures previously taken... are being reviewed to assess which of the previous measures need to be revived in the present situation," Tarar said.Pakistan had introduced the measures on March 9 as oil prices surged during the US-Iran war.The steps included halving fuel allowances for official vehicles, reducing lawmakers' salaries and allowing public sector employees to work from home for part of the week.The measures were withdrawn in June after the US and Iran entered a peace process. But renewed hostilities have once again pushed up international oil prices, putting pressure on fuel-importing countries such as Pakistan.Some restrictions, including shorter market hours, are already continuing, Tarar said.The government is facing the renewed pressure as petrol prices have climbed to PKR 375.82 per litre and high-speed diesel to PKR 403.32 per litre.To cushion the impact on smaller vehicle users, the government has announced a relief of Rs 100 per litre for motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqi three-wheelers and vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.Tarar said Sharif had asked deputy PM and foreign minister Ishaq Dar to make sure transport fares did not rise after the relief scheme was introduced.
Article Summary: Pakistan may bring back austerity measures to reduce fuel consumption as renewed fighting in West Asia drives up global oil prices. PM Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to examine which of the measures introduced earlier this year can be brought back. Measures included halving fuel allowances for official vehicles, reducing lawmakers' salaries and allowing public sector employees to work from home.

Article Title: IMF team to visit Pakistan for crucial $7-bn bailout review, next tranche in focus
Article Text:
IMF returns to Pakistan for crucial $7 bn bailout review

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is set to return to Pakistan on September 23 for a crucial review of its $7 billion bailout programme, with the outcome likely to determine the release of the next tranche and shape Islamabad’s economic policy in the months ahead.The mission, led by Iva Petrova, is expected to stay for almost two weeks, with discussions continuing into the first week of October, Dawn reported. The review will cover Pakistan’s economic performance and implementation of the EFF for the period ending June 30, 2026. The IMF will also conduct the third review of the $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).The visit is expected to begin with technical discussions at the State Bank of Pakistan, followed by meetings with government sectoral teams and an inaugural meeting with finance minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, according to official sources cited by Dawn.Pakistan has taken 25 arrangements with the IMF since joining the Fund. As of September 11, its total IMF credit outstanding stood at SDR 8.026 billion, making it the third-largest IMF debtor after Argentina and Ukraine.Pakistan is more than halfway through the 37-month Extended Fund Facility approved by the IMF Board of Directors in September 2024.The IMF delegation will examine fiscal and monetary policies, growth prospects, external finances and risks, as well as Pakistan’s implementation of programme commitments.A key focus will be the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) preparedness to meet its first half-yearly revenue collection structural benchmark under an IMF programme.Dawn reported that revenue shortfalls, commodity-market interventions and delays in economic governance reforms remain among the issues under scrutiny. The newspaper said official reports indicate that only a few of more than three dozen governance-related targets for January-June 2026 had been met.IMF resident representative for Pakistan Mahir Binici, however, said in July that the country’s performance under the 2024 EFF had been “strong so far”, according to a press release issued by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute and cited by Dawn.The IMF’s Executive Board completed Pakistan’s third EFF review and second RSF review in May, releasing about $1.1 billion under the EFF and around $220 million under the RSF. Total disbursements under the two arrangements reached about $4.8 billion, the IMF said.The September review will determine whether Pakistan remains on track for the next disbursement.
Article Summary: The International Monetary Fund is set to return to Pakistan on September 23 for a crucial review of its $7 billion bailout programme. The mission, led by Iva Petrova, is expected to stay for almost two weeks, with discussions continuing into the first week of October. Review will cover Pakistan’s economic performance and implementation of the EFF for the period ending June 30, 2026.

Article Title: Balochistan on edge: BLF claims string of attacks on Pakistani military convoys, camps
Article Text: The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has claimed responsibility for a string of attacks targeting Pakistani security forces across Balochistan, including alleged ambushes on military convoys, attacks on camps and the seizure of weapons, according to a report.BLF spokesperson Gwahram Baloch said group's fighters carried out several operations between September 1 and 11 across areas including Kharan, Kech, Tump and Dasht.According to the statement cited by the Balochistan Post, BLF fighters stopped and searched vehicles at a checkpoint in Koh Dagar, Mand, on September 11. The group said the move was aimed at maintaining its presence and tracking the movements of Pakistani forces and people it described as their local facilitators.Meanwhile, Pakistan’s authorities have claimed that nine militants were killed in separate security operations in Balochistan. Palistan police said six were killed in an exchange of fire with Counter Terrorism Department personnel in Pishin’s Saranan area, while four security personnel were injured. In another operation, three militants, including wanted militant Naqeebullah, were allegedly killed after their vehicle was targeted in a quadcopter strike in Mastung on Sunday.A day earlier, the BLF claimed it attacked a military convoy in Tatgar, Yakmach, in Kharan. The group alleged that two buses carrying Pakistani military personnel were hit by heavy and automatic weapons, killing six personnel and injuring several others. The claims have not been independently verified.The BLF further claimed that Pakistani forces launched a pursuit operation in the Hermag desert following the attack but withdrew after encountering resistance.The group also reported another checkpoint operation on the Nasirabad-Nodiz highway in Kech on September 10. It alleged that Pakistani military convoys and quadcopters later reached the area and carried out aerial firing after BLF fighters had left.In Tump, the organisation claimed attacks were carried out against military camps in Dil Kik, Zamuran and Rodbun. According to TBP, the BLF said heavy weapons, grenade launchers and automatic firearms were used and that the attacks caused casualties and material damage.The group also claimed that its fighters intercepted the official vehicle of Tump's assistant commissioner in Khairabad, Turbat, on September 9. It said the official escaped in another vehicle, while weapons and equipment belonging to his security detail were taken.The BLF referred to an earlier attack in Pattok, Dasht, on September 1, claiming that a military patrol was targeted, one vehicle was damaged and several personnel were killed or wounded.The latest statement follows earlier BLF claims covering attacks between August and September 9. The group had claimed that more than 12 Pakistani military personnel and one police officer were killed in 11 operations across Chagai, Surab, Awaran, Khuzdar, Rakhshan, Kech, Quetta and Barkhan.On September 9, the BLF also claimed that its fighters took control of the Talaran police station in Chagai's Baramcha area, detained police personnel and seized weapons, equipment and a vehicle. It said the personnel were later released unharmed after being warned.The group had separately claimed that 97 Pakistani military personnel were killed and 15 seriously injured in 48 operations across 23 locations in Balochistan in July.
Article Summary: The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has claimed responsibility for a string of attacks targeting Pakistani security forces. The group's fighters carried out several operations between September 1 and 11 across areas including Kharan, Kech, Tump and Dasht. Pakistan’s authorities have claimed that nine militants were killed in separate security operations.

Article Title: Munir fails Mecca test: Why Pakistan’s Field Marshal is not riding to rescue MBS
Article Text:
Mecca Pact faces first test as Pakistan hesitates to fight Houthis in support of Saudi Arabia. (Asim Munir: AP image)

Why it matters:

The Mecca Pact is a trilateral defence alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan aimed at strengthening regional security and collective deterrence.

Catch up quick

Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement in September 2025 and expanded it into the three-way Mecca Pact in August 2026, with a joint secretariat based in Riyadh and Pakistan holding the first three-year chairmanship, Al Jazeera reported.

The pact has never been invoked. Pakistan's defense minister, Khawaja Asif, said this week that an unprovoked attack on Saudi Arabia or a spillover of the Yemen war would make the Mecca agreement operational, adding, "there should be no doubt in this," though he gave no specifics on what that would look like in practice.

Turkey's foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, has compared the pact's mechanics to NATO's, under which an attacked member requests specific help rather than triggering automatic intervention.

There is not much clarity on when a Mecca pact member would seek help from others: Under what circumstance, an attack on a member would be regarded as an attack on all members?

It is not clear whether Saudi Arabia has asked for Pakistan’s help in its fight against Houthis. As per an Axios report, MBS did reach out to US President Donald Trump to seek US help against Houthis. But Trump declined to come to Saudi Crown Prince’s rescue.

Importantly, this isn't the first time Pakistan would be failing Saudi Arabia militarily. In 2015, Pakistan's parliament unanimously rejected King Salman's request to send troops into the Saudi-led coalition against the Houthis.

Between the lines

The Houthis are an armed political and religious group from Yemen who have been locked in a long-running military conflict with the Saudi government.

The battlefield problem

The bottom line:

As Houthi forces seized Mokha and Perim Island last week, Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir spent the moment on the phone with Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi.Munir seems in no hurry to mobilise Pakistan military against Saudi Arabia's attackers.Saudi Arabia’s Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) planned the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Pakistan and Turkey specifically as insurance against a moment like this one.Yet the pact's first real test is exposing how little Riyadh can actually count on Islamabad, whose army chief has far stronger incentives to stay out of a shooting war with Tehran than to jump into one on Saudi Arabia's behalf.Pakistan relies heavily on Saudi Arabia and the Gulf for foreign exchange, investment, energy support and financial assistance.That dependence cuts in Riyadh's favour on paper but works against a real Pakistani commitment in practice.As per reports, Pakistan already has roughly 16 JF-17 fighters, air-defense units and thousands of troops stationed in Saudi Arabia under earlier bilateral arrangements, which lets Munir point to a visible Pakistani footprint in the kingdom without ever having to fire a shot at the Houthis.But Munir has good reasons to hedge that have nothing to do with sentiment toward Riyadh. Pakistan shares a long, porous border with Iran and has its own security concerns there.Joining a campaign against the Houthis could turn Pakistan’s support for Riyadh into a confrontation with Iran and its partners.Pakistan also has a sizeable Shia population and may face domestic opposition if it intervenes directly in Saudi Arabia-Houthi fight.There's also a Washington dimension complicating things. Munir has spent the past year cultivating Donald Trump. With Trump having twice rejected Saudi requests for US strikes on the Houthis, Munir is unlikely to take a position that could put him at odds with the US president, especially on an issue where Trump has already made his position clear.Even a willing Pakistan could not easily repair the military and political weaknesses exposed in Yemen. The Houthis’ advance was enabled partly by divisions among their opponents.Saudi-backed forces failed to cooperate effectively during the offensive. The withdrawal of the UAE also deprived the coalition of a capable supporter and deepened problems with southern factions.Additional Pakistani aircraft would not automatically resolve rival chains of command, competing territorial ambitions or distrust between local forces.Would Pakistan be defending Saudi airspace, reopening shipping lanes, recovering territory or helping impose a settlement? Each objective entails different resources and risks.MBS signed the Mecca Pact to buy himself military insurance against exactly the kind of Iranian-aligned assault now unfolding on his coastline.But Munir's incentives point toward mediating the Houthi crisis from Tehran's side of the table, not fighting it from Riyadh's, leaving Saudi Arabia's newest ally looking a lot more like a hedge than a rescue plan.(With inputs from agencies)
Article Summary: Mecca Pact is a trilateral defence alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan. Pakistan's defense minister said an unprovoked attack on Saudi Arabia or a spillover of the Yemen war would make the Mecca agreement operational. It is not clear whether Saudi Arabia has asked for Pakistan’s help in its fight against Houthis.

Article Title: Pakistan lists Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar as fugitive, hikes bounty ahead of FATF review
Article Text:
Masood Azhar listed as 'fugitive'

NEW DELHI: Pakistan has raised the bounty on Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar to PKR 70 lakh and listed him as a fugitive in its latest Red Book of most wanted terrorists, news agency ANI reported citing sources.The development comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) plenary scheduled for October, with Pakistan seeking to avoid being placed back on the global watchdog's grey list.Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has increased the reward for information leading to most-wanted terrorist Azhar's capture by PKR 20 lakh. The agency had announced a PKR 50 lakh bounty on him in 2021.Sources told ANI that Pakistan's latest move is aimed at projecting action against terrorism ahead of the FATF review.Pakistan had claimed in 2021 that Azhar was no longer in the country and had fled to Afghanistan. The Shehbaz Sharif-led government has since maintained that the JeM chief is not on Pakistani soil.Five years after announcing the initial bounty, the FIA has now raised it to PKR 70 lakh and included Azhar in its latest Red Book of most wanted terrorists.However, the decision of declaring Azhar as 'fugitive' comes merely to mislead the global community and hide sheltered-terror outfits on its soil.In October, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif is also scheduled to meet US President Donald Trump on UNGA sidelines.Masood Azhar-led Jaish stands responsible for numerous terror attacks in India, including Parliament attack that took place in 2001.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has increased the reward for information leading to most-wanted terrorist Azhar's capture by PKR 20 lakh. The agency had announced a PKR 50 lakh bounty on him in 2021. Pakistan had claimed in 2021 that Azhar was no longer in the country and had fled to Afghanistan.

Article Title: Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pakistan expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on kingdom
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif with Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud

Sharif vows to support peace efforts

Defence pact comes into focus

Houthi attacks and Red Sea escalation

The Mecca pact may promise “one for all, all for one”, but Pakistan is not putting boots on the ground just yet.Islamabad on Sunday expressed “complete solidarity” with Saudi Arabia after a fresh wave of Houthi attacks on the kingdom, while warning that the strikes could threaten regional security and further disrupt global energy supplies.Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif conveyed Pakistan’s support to Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman during a phone call, according to the Pakistan Prime Minister’s Office.The outreach came a day after Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 1,200-km East-West oil pipeline following a drone attack launched from Iraq.The pipeline is an important alternative route for Saudi oil exports as it allows crude to reach the Red Sea without passing through the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping has been severely disrupted by the wider US-Iran conflict since February.“While expressing complete solidarity with the Saudi leadership as well as the brotherly people of Saudi Arabia, the Prime Minister stated that the recent Houthi actions threatened regional peace and security and could further disrupt the global economy and energy supplies,” the Pakistan PMO said.Sharif condemned what he described as Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian and economic infrastructure, saying such strikes could further affect the global economy and energy supplies.He also said he, Pakistan’s army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar would continue efforts to reduce tensions and restore peace in West Asia.The Saudi crown prince appreciated Islamabad’s efforts towards peace and stability in the region, according to the PMO statement. The two leaders agreed to remain in close contact and expressed hope of meeting soon.The latest Houthi attacks have added to concerns over the security of Saudi energy infrastructure and alternative oil export routes amid wider disruption to regional shipping.The developments have also revived attention on a mutual-defence pact signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7.Under the agreement, an armed attack against any one of the three countries would effectively be regarded as an attack against all three, with the pact also providing for enhanced defence cooperation.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif had said on Wednesday that there should be no ambiguity over the commitment under the arrangement. He said an unprovoked attack on a member, or the spillover of the conflict in Yemen into Saudi Arabia, could activate the pact’s collective-defence provisions.However, Pakistan’s foreign ministry later clarified that no military response under the agreement was currently being discussed.Foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said, “There is no such thing under discussion right now ... When time comes (we) will act under the agreement.”Pakistan also said there were no immediate plans to expand the Mecca defence alliance.The Houthi attacks have intensified as the Iran-backed Yemeni group has advanced along the Red Sea coast.According to news agency AP, the Houthis claimed further missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, while Saudi civil defence said a projectile fell in al-Tawwal governorate near the Yemen border, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings.A Houthi military spokesperson, Brig Gen Yahya Saree, claimed that the group had targeted a military base in Saudi Arabia’s Najran region, although he provided no evidence or details on when the attack occurred.The escalation has also affected Yemen. The internationally recognised Yemeni government has vowed to regroup and fight back after the Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and other areas along the west coast.The International Organisation for Migration said more than 85,000 people had been displaced by the fighting since the beginning of the month, while more than 2,000 Yemenis had reached Djibouti after crossing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.The Houthi advance has heightened concerns over the security of the Bab el-Mandeb, a crucial shipping route linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, at a time when the wider regional conflict has already disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif conveyed Pakistan’s support to Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman during a phone call. The outreach came a day after Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 1,200-km East-West oil pipeline following a drone attack from Iraq.

Article Title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to meet Donald Trump on September 23 during UNGA in New York: Report
Article Text:
Pak PM to meet Trump on UNGA sidelines

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is set to meet US President Donald Trump in New York on September 23 during the United Nations General Assembly week, according to a media report cited by news agency PTI.Sharif is among the world leaders invited to a reception dinner being hosted by Trump and First Lady Melania Trump on September 23, The News reported, citing high-level sources.The event is scheduled at the Lotte New York Palace Hotel on Madison Avenue.The dinner could give Sharif an opportunity to hold discussions with Trump as well as other heads of state and government attending the UNGA.The proposed meeting comes months after the two leaders met at the inaugural Board of Peace meeting in Washington in February. They had previously held talks at the White House in September 2025 and met again during the Sharm el-Sheikh Peace Summit in Egypt in October last year.Sharif is expected to arrive in New York on September 22 and address the UN General Assembly on September 25. According to the report, he is likely to use his address to raise Pakistan's concerns over India's decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.India suspended the 1960 treaty in April 2025 following the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 civilians.New Delhi said the pact would remain in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably ended its support for crossborder terrorism.The Indus Waters Treaty, brokered by the World Bank, sets out the framework for sharing the waters of six rivers in the Indus river system between the two countries.Sharif is also expected to speak about Pakistan's new security partnership with Saudi Arabia and Turkey. The three countries signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, creating a collective defence framework under which an attack on one member would be considered an attack on all three.The 81st UN General Assembly's high-level General Debate will be held from September 22 to 26 and on September 28 at the UN headquarters in New York. Sharif is scheduled to speak fourth during the second half of the session on September 25.Shehbaz Sharif's proposed meeting with Trump comes against the backdrop of India's diplomatic engagement with major global powers, highlighted by the Brics Summit 2026 hosted by New Delhi.The summit brought together leaders including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, underlining India's role in engaging with key powers across geopolitical blocs.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also announced the unanimous adoption of the New Delhi Declaration by Brics leaders.The summit also saw Brics leaders condemn the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir. In their joint statement, the leaders reaffirmed their commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and called for a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism.
Article Summary: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif is set to meet US President Donald Trump in New York on September 23. The two leaders will attend a reception dinner being hosted by Trump and First Lady Melania Trump. The proposed meeting comes months after the two leaders met at the inaugural Board of Peace meeting in Washington in February.

Article Title: Pakistan blinks on Houthis, walks back Saudi defence warning within 24 hours
Article Text:
Pakistan has clarified that there are no current discussions about military responses related to the Mecca defense pact, following recent warnings from its defense minister.

No plans to expand Mecca pact

Pakistan appears to have taken a step back from its strong warning to the Houthis a day earlier, with Islamabad on Thursday saying that no military response under the newly signed Mecca defence pact is currently being discussed. The comments came despite its defence minister warning that the agreement could become operational if the Yemen conflict spilled into Saudi Arabia.“There is no such thing under discussion right now ... When time comes (we) will act under the agreement,” Pakistan foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Thursday, referring to the pact signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month.The apparent shift comes a day after defence minister Khawaja Asif warned that the pact could become operational if the Yemen conflict spilled into Saudi Arabia. He said Pakistan was “bound by the terms and conditions of this pact” and would honour its commitments if required.Asif had also warned the Houthis that if they tried to extend the Yemen conflict into Saudi Arabia, “the clauses of this pact over confronting aggression will become operative”. At the same time, he stressed that the agreement was defensive and did not authorise the three countries to independently launch offensive operations against another country.The latest clarification comes as Houthi attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure have intensified.The Mecca joint defence agreement was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7 in Mecca to strengthen collective deterrence and defence cooperation. Under the agreement, “any armed attack against any one of the three States shall be regarded as an attack against them all.” The pact also calls for enhanced defence cooperation among the three countries.Pakistan also ruled out any immediate expansion of the Mecca defence alliance, with foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan saying “there are no plans to expand the Mecca alliance.”The clarification comes after earlier discussions about potentially bringing other countries into the arrangement. Pakistan's foreign ministry had previously said that any country seeking to join would be considered in consultation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, but that there were no formal applications or new names at that stage.
Article Summary: Pakistan says there are no current discussions about military responses to the Mecca defense pact. Defence minister Khawaja Asif had warned that the pact could become operational if the Yemen conflict spilled into Saudi Arabia. The Mecca joint defence agreement was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7.

Article Title: Osama bin Laden had Taliban rival assassinated 2 days before 9/11 attack
Article Text:
Osama bin Laden (File photo)

Ahmad Shah Massoud, the prominent Afghan resistance leader and one of the Taliban's strongest rivals, was assassinated on September 9, 2001, just two days before the 9/11 attacks, in a killing believed to have been ordered by al-Qaeda chief Osama bin Laden as a favour to his Taliban hosts, according to a Newsweek report.Massoud, who led Afghanistan's Northern Alliance, was killed while being interviewed at his camp in the Panjshir Valley by two men posing as Belgian television journalists. The two al-Qaeda operatives had concealed explosives inside a video camera despite undergoing security checks before meeting the resistance leader, Newsweek reported.The Northern Alliance did not officially confirm Massoud's death until September 15.Massoud had built a powerful insurgent network in northern Afghanistan and remained a major obstacle to Taliban control of the country. His influence and popularity also made him a key figure among forces opposed to the Taliban.According to Newsweek, bin Laden was believed to have ordered Massoud's assassination partly as a favour to his Taliban hosts and partly because he expected the United States to launch retaliatory strikes following the planned September 11 attacks Eliminating Massoud was also strategically important because bin Laden understood the Afghan leader's value as a military commander and political figure who could have played a significant role in any campaign against the Taliban and al-Qaeda.The assassination alarmed the CIA, which had maintained contacts with Massoud and other Afghan opposition figures.Gary Berntsen, the CIA officer who later led the agency's first team into Afghanistan after the 9/11 attacks, recalled that the news "made me feel sick to my stomach ... I figured this was the end of the Northern Alliance."CIA director George Tenet was less pessimistic, noting that the agency had maintained relationships with other Afghan warlords.Tenet later wrote, "Masood's [sic] brutal murder by al-Qaeda on the eve of the 9/11 attacks might have undone our plan before it got under way if we hadn't maintained contact with other warlords in the north."Tenet's meeting with Pakistan's ISI chiefOn the day Massoud was assassinated, Tenet was having lunch with Pakistani Gen.
