Mahmood Ahmed, then head of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Pakistan's main intelligence agency.According to Tenet's account, he pressed Mahmood on al-Qaeda and Taliban leader Mullah Omar. Mahmood assured him that Omar wanted what was best for the Afghan people and suggested that the CIA try bribing key Taliban officials to secure bin Laden's surrender."As gracious as he could be over the lunch table, the guy was immovable when it came to the Taliban and al-Qaeda," Tenet later wrote.Mahmood would be in Washington on September 11, when he met senior US lawmakers including Senate Intelligence Committee chairman Bob Graham, House Intelligence Committee chairman Porter Goss and Senator Jon Kyl.In the aftermath of the attacks, Mahmood held further meetings with US officials as Washington pressed Pakistan to cooperate in its campaign against terrorism. US military forces were also clandestinely deployed to Pakistani territory as the Bush administration prepared its response to the attacks.Massoud's assassination therefore came at a critical moment. Two days before the attacks that transformed US foreign policy and triggered the war in Afghanistan, one of the Taliban's most formidable opponents had already been eliminated.
Article Summary: Ahmad Shah Massoud was assassinated on September 9, 2001, two days before the 9/11 attacks. Massoud led Afghanistan's Northern Alliance and was a major obstacle to Taliban control. Al-Qaeda chief Osama bin Laden believed to have ordered Massoud's assassination.

Article Title: 5 bodies found after Indian, Nepal teams use ‘rat-hole’ digging in Chilime tunnel
Article Text:
Six workers were believed trapped inside after the Aug 26 disaster, and search continued for the remaining worker.

Five bodies were recovered from Nepal’s flood-buried Chilime hydropower project on Wednesday after specialised Indian Army personnel and Nepalese rescuers reached its underground powerhouse by digging the final stretch by hand when excavators and wheel loaders could advance no farther. Six workers were believed trapped inside after the Aug 26 disaster, and search continued for the remaining worker.The operation began in severely waterlogged conditions and the team used safety ropes and improvised floats to enter the tunnel. Heavy machinery subsequently cleared much of the mud, boulders and debris, but rescuers had to adopt a rat-hole-style technique to manually cut through the final 35 metres of an approximately 150-metre obstruction leading towards the powerhouse.The method resembled the manual excavation used during the 2023 Silkyara tunnel rescue in Uttarakhand, where rat-hole miners cleared the final portion after drilling machinery became ineffective. At Chilime too, personnel crawled into the restricted space and removed debris by hand as teams outside carried it away.Hopes of finding survivors had briefly risen after engineer Shriram Neupane reported what appeared to be voices or echoes from deeper inside the tunnel.“We are expecting some good news,” Neupane had said on Monday, expressing confidence that a breakthrough was expected within hours.Ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party MP and engineer Sagar Dhakal, who worked alongside rescue teams for several days, said, “I tried my best as an MP, engineer, Nepali and a normal human being, leaving no stone unturned. I carried the heavy load where it was necessary to carry it, and I was the labourer where it was necessary to be."Dhakal said the operation repeatedly ran into technical setbacks before teams found a way through. He thanked Chilime engineers, Nepal Army, Indian Army, Nepal Electricity Authority personnel and locals for working around the clock.The floods had also hit 12 hydropower projects in Nepal — eight operational plants with 281MW capacity and four under construction with 388MW capacity. The disaster has so far left 1,442 people dead and around 5,719 missing across Nepal and Tibet.
Article Summary: Five bodies were recovered from Nepal’s flood-buried Chilime hydropower project. Six workers were believed trapped inside after the Aug 26 disaster. The disaster has so far left 1,442 people dead and around 5,719 missing across Nepal and Tibet.

Article Title: UAE cancels visas of thousands of Bangladeshis amid heightened scrutiny
Article Text:
Bangladeshi expatriates in the UAE are facing unexpected visa cancellations, which has left many in a state of uncertainty (Photo: Rashed Sumon)

The UAE has cancelled the visas of thousands of Bangladeshis, leaving many expatriates stranded in Bangladesh and unable to return to their jobs, businesses and families in the Gulf country. Bangladesh has taken up the issue with the UAE through diplomatic channels and sought a review of the cancellations.The Daily Star reported that the number of affected Bangladeshis has risen from around 4,000 to 4,800, citing Bangladeshi ministry sources. However, the UAE has not publicly confirmed the figure. Bangladesh’s foreign ministry had said on July 30 that 626 Bangladeshis had faced automatic visa cancellations, while stressing that the cancellations were not specific to Bangladesh and had also affected nationals of other countries.Many affected Bangladeshis had returned home on leave before receiving cancellation notices by email or mobile message. Abul Kalam Azad, who had lived in the UAE for 27 years, told The Daily Star that he returned to Bangladesh on April 7 and received a visa cancellation email on July 24 without any reason being given.The cancellations have affected both workers and business owners. One Bangladeshi told The Daily Star that he had two businesses in the UAE and a wife living in Dubai, but was now unable to return.The UAE is home to around 1.2 million Bangladeshi expatriates, according to Bangladesh’s foreign ministry. Dhaka has been seeking greater mobility and the reopening of labour visas for Bangladeshi nationals.The reasons behind the latest cancellations remain unclear. MS Shekil Chowdhury, chairman of the Centre for Non-Resident Bangladeshi, said UAE authorities had increased scrutiny amid the wider Middle East conflict, including checks related to visa renewals, documentation and social media activity. He stressed that he was not saying these factors directly caused the cancellations.Bangladesh’s expatriates’ welfare ministry has asked recently affected Bangladeshis to submit their details as the government works to establish the scale of the problem. Affected expatriates have also sought financial assistance, rehabilitation and diplomatic intervention to help them return to their previous workplaces.The Bangladesh government has not announced a final number of affected nationals or a confirmed reason for the visa cancellations.
Article Summary: Bangladesh has taken up the issue with the UAE through diplomatic channels. The number of affected Bangladeshis has risen from around 4,000 to 4,800. The UAE is home to around 1.2 million Bangladeshi expatriates, according to Bangladesh’s foreign ministry.

Article Title: Bangladesh tribunal sentences seven Awami League members to death over 'July uprising'
Article Text: Dhaka: Bangladesh International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Tuesday sentenced seven Awami League leaders, including party general secretary and former minister Obaidul Quader, to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July 2024 mass uprising that led to the ouster of Sheikh Hasina as prime minister.Like Hasina and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, who were also sentenced to death for crimes against humanity in Nov last year, they were also tried in absentia by the three-member tribunal headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury."The only thing we have to fear is fear itself. They have been creating an atmosphere of fear, feeling an existential threat to power. Dec is not too far," Quader said in a post on Facebook after the verdict, referring to Awami League chief Hasina announcing that she would return to Bangladesh in Dec to put the country on the "right track" as she is undeterred by the threat of imprisonment or a death sentence.The other convicts are party joint general secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim and executive committee member Mohammad Ali Arafat; Jubo League chairperson Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and Jubo League general secretary Md Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil; and Bangladesh Chhatra League president Md Saddam Hossain and its general secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Inan.ICT also ordered confiscation of 50% of movable and immovable properties of Quader, Nasim, Arafat, Parash and Nikhil. It also ordered that compensation be provided to those killed or injured during the uprising, or their families, from the proceeds of sale of the confiscated properties through the July Foundation or another statutory organisation.
Article Summary: Seven Awami League leaders sentenced to death for crimes against humanity. Crimes committed during the July 2024 mass uprising that led to the ouster of Sheikh Hasina as prime minister. Former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal and former party general secretary Obaidul Quader also convicted.
